spark_scene.description: True-color satellite view of the main Hawaiian Islands from the northwestern islands to the large southeastern island, showing dark ocean with scattered white cumulus clouds and translucent gray haze extending west and southwest of the islands.

plumes.label: large gray haze west of southeastern island
plumes.visual_description: broad diffuse light-gray translucent haze blanket extending west and southwest from the west coast of the large southeastern island over the ocean

plumes.label: elongated gray streak west of central islands
plumes.visual_description: long narrow light-gray translucent streak extending west-southwest from the vicinity of the central small islands

plumes.label: faint gray streak west of north-central island
plumes.visual_description: small faint gray-white translucent wedge extending west from the western tip of the north-central island

firms.source: NASA GIBS FIRMS thermal anomaly layers (2023-08-08), rasterised
firms.note: counts are rendered marker pixels on a 0.005-deg grid, not individual detections
firms.volcanic_note: summit-caldera thermal detections (active vent glow), excluded from fire clusters

volcano_status.source: USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory notices via HANS public API (https://volcanoes.usgs.gov/hans-public/api/search/search)

kilauea.activity_summary: Kīlauea volcano is not erupting. No significant changes have been observed at the summit or in either rift zone over the past week.

evidence: Both volcanoes not erupting at image time: Kilauea ADVISORY/YELLOW 'is not erupting', Mauna Loa NORMAL/GREEN 'no', ruling against vog. [E1]
Multiple large wildfire clusters on Hawai'i Island west side: Kailua-Kona clusters n=206 and n=46, plus n=21 near Mauna Loa summit slopes, providing smoke source on west coast. [E5]
Plume 1 upwind end far from vents: 277.8 km to Kilauea, 246.8 km to Mauna Loa, inconsistent with vog point source. [E9]
Mask is 0.1% land over ocean west/southwest of Hawai'i Island, a diffuse translucent gray blanket over ocean, not white cumulus cloud. [E6, E2]
Volcanoes not erupting, so elongated gray streak is not vog despite downwind location. [E1]
Very large fire cluster at Kula, Maui (3 km) n=201, the dominant fire in the scene, co-located with streak origin. [E5]
result.source_hint: 2023-08-08 Maui/Hawai'i wildfire outbreak (Lahaina fires), not volcanic vog

result.caveats: Winds at plume 1 location are westerly (from 272 deg) likely due to island wake/lee eddy south-west of Hawai'i Island, so transport direction there is less clean than the NE trades at plumes 2-3; plume 3 is very faint and small so cloud vs thin smoke cannot be fully excluded.

overall.rule: most hazardous class with confidence >= 0.70 (wildfire_smoke > vog_* > dust > cloud)
